items.scope: Finite instance S3 (permutations of 3 elements), explicitly a finite test instance, not the Monster.
items.statement: The finite test instance S3 has a two-sided identity element e with e*x = x*e = x for every element x.

items.scope: Finite instance S3 only, not the Monster.
items.statement: The finite test instance S3 is closed under composition: the product of any two of its 6 elements is again one of the 6 elements.

items.scope: Finite instance S3 only (all 216 triples), not the Monster.
items.statement: Composition in the finite test instance S3 is associative: (a*b)*c = a*(b*c) for all triples a, b, c.

items.scope: Finite instance S3 only, not the Monster.
items.statement: Every element of the finite test instance S3 has a two-sided inverse inside S3.

items.scope: Finite instance: an explicit map between the two small groups S3 and C2 only.
items.statement: The sign map from S3 to the two-element group {+1, -1} under multiplication is a group homomorphism: sign(a*b) = sign(a)*sign(b) for all pairs.

items.scope: Finite instance S3 only; this is a deliberate negative test, so the expected status is COUNTEREXAMPLE.
items.statement: The constant map from S3 to S3 sending every element to the transposition (1,0,2) is NOT a homomorphism; a checker must detect the failure and exhibit a counterexample pair. The expected checker outcome is that the homomorphism property fails.

items.scope: Finite instance S3 character table only; no claim about Monster characters is checked here.
items.statement: The irreducible characters of S3 (trivial, sign, and the 2-dimensional standard character chi(p) = fix(p) - 1) are constant on conjugacy classes and pairwise orthonormal under the class-weighted inner product; the dimensions satisfy 1^2 + 1^2 + 2^2 = 6 = |S3|.

items.scope: Finite instance S3 only, not the Monster.
items.statement: The conjugacy classes of S3 partition the group, with class sizes 1, 2, 3 summing to 6 (the class equation for S3).

items.scope: UNSUPPORTED for machine check here: no enumeration or direct check of the Monster is performed; its order makes exhaustive enumeration impossible and no validated Monster character table or generator set is an input to this package. The finite checks above concern S3 only and prove nothing about the Monster.
items.statement: The Monster group itself (its group axioms on its own elements, its representation homomorphisms, character table, and conjugacy classes) is a well-defined mathematical object of order approximately 8.08e53.

families.title: Monster Group (finite-instance checks plus abstract-only Monster items)

items.scope: Data-check against the established published values {744, 196884, 21493760, 864299970} only; the checker compares the values recorded in this file against the published table it carries and verifies exact integer equality.
items.statement: The normalised J-function has q-expansion J = q^-1 + 744 + 196884 q + 21493760 q^2 + 864299970 q^3 + ... with the stated established published coefficients.

items.scope: Established published identity, checked as exact integer arithmetic. Checking the arithmetic does not prove the representation-theoretic statement; it verifies the recorded numbers are consistent.
items.statement: McKay's identity: 196884 = 196883 + 1, where 196883 is the dimension of the smallest nontrivial irreducible representation of the Monster and 1 is the trivial dimension.

items.scope: Data-check against established published irreducible dimensions {1, 196883, 21296876, 842609326}; exact integer sums only. This verifies the recorded decompositions arithmetically, not the moonshine correspondence itself.
items.statement: The next J coefficients decompose into Monster irreducible dimensions (with multiplicities) as 21493760 = 1 + 196883 + 21296876 and 864299970 = 2*1 + 2*196883 + 21296876 + 842609326.

items.scope: UNSUPPORTED for machine check here: modular invariance is a statement about an analytic function on the upper half-plane; no modular-forms library is an input to this package and the identity is not machine-verified here.
items.statement: The J-function is invariant under the modular transformations generated by S: tau -> -1/tau and T: tau -> tau + 1.

items.scope: UNSUPPORTED for machine check here: this is the full moonshine correspondence, far beyond the concrete coefficient identities above; it is not machine-verified here and no part of it is checked by the finite or data checks in this package.
items.statement: For each Monster element g, the McKay-Thompson series T_g is the normalised Hauptmodul of a genus-zero group.

items.scope: UNSUPPORTED for machine check here: the statement quantifies over infinitely many graded pieces and requires the vertex-operator-algebra machinery; no finite truncation checked here would establish it, so it is recorded as abstract-only.
items.statement: Graded dimensions of the moonshine module satisfy the partition-function constraints imposed by its vertex-operator-algebra structure.

families.title: Monstrous Moonshine (published-data checks plus abstract-only theory items)

items.scope: Concrete small algebra so(3) only; the stored bracket table is compared entry-by-entry against the Levi-Civita definition over the rationals.
items.statement: The so(3)-type bracket on a 3-dimensional real basis {e0, e1, e2} has structure constants given by the Levi-Civita symbol: [e_i, e_j] = sum_k eps_ijk e_k, with eps_012 = eps_120 = eps_201 = +1, eps_021 = eps_102 = eps_210 = -1, and eps_ijk = 0 whenever two indices coincide.

items.scope: Concrete small algebra so(3) only, computed exactly over the rationals; max residual 0 expected.
items.statement: The so(3) bracket is antisymmetric: [x, y] = -[y, x] for all basis pairs (and hence for all vectors by bilinearity).

items.scope: Concrete small algebra so(3) only, all 27 basis triples computed exactly over the rationals; max residual 0 expected.
items.statement: The so(3) bracket satisfies the Jacobi identity: [x, [y, z]] + [y, [z, x]] + [z, [x, y]] = 0 for all basis triples.

items.scope: Named finite action only (C4 acting on 4 vertices, all 64 triples checked). This is a finite instance of the action law, not a check of any positive-dimensional Lie group action.
items.statement: Group-action composition holds for the named finite action of the cyclic group C4 (rotations by quarter turns) on the four vertices of a square: (g + h) . v = g . (h . v), and 0 . v = v, for all g, h in C4 and all vertices v.

items.scope: UNSUPPORTED for machine check here: tangent spaces and left translation are differential-geometric constructions requiring smooth-manifold machinery that is not an input to this package; the finite so(3) bracket checks above do not verify this item.
items.statement: The tangent space at the identity of a Lie group carries the Lie bracket of its Lie algebra and is consistent under left translation.

items.scope: UNSUPPORTED for machine check here: equivariance for smooth actions needs differential geometry (smooth maps between manifolds); only the finite C4 action law above is machine-checked, and it does not establish this item.
items.statement: Lie group actions on manifolds are equivariant with respect to the relevant structure maps.

items.scope: UNSUPPORTED for machine check here: chart compatibility is a statement about smooth atlases; no atlas or transition-function data is an input to this package.
items.statement: Coordinate transformations between overlapping charts of a manifold are compatible on overlaps (cocycle condition).

families.title: Lie Groups and Manifolds (exact finite checks on so(3) plus abstract-only geometry items)

items.scope: Bounded scope: one concrete dyadic grid, exact rational arithmetic. Evidence for this grid only, not a proof for arbitrary subdivisions.
items.statement: On a concrete dyadic quadtree subdivision of the unit square to depth 2, every parent cell measure equals the sum of its four children measures, exactly, and the 16 leaf measures sum to 1.

items.scope: Bounded scope: the stated transform and test vectors only. Evidence for this instance, not a proof for arbitrary transforms.
items.statement: The concrete integer shear transform T(x, y) = (x + 2y, y) on Z^2 and its inverse T^-1(x, y) = (x - 2y, y) compose to the identity on a stated set of test vectors, with residual 0.

items.scope: Bounded scope: the stated concrete shapes only; a shape invariant on these shapes, not a theorem about arbitrary tensors.
items.statement: For the concrete tensor shape (2, 3, 4), transposition to (4, 3, 2) and reshapes to (6, 4) and (24,) preserve the total element count 24 and the number of entries is the product of the dimensions in every stated shape.

items.scope: Bounded scope: numerical evidence on the stated signal and grid only; a floating-point residual is numerical evidence, never a proof.
items.statement: Linear-interpolation upsampling of a concrete sampled signal on a dyadic grid, followed by downsampling at the original sample points, reconstructs the samples with maximum absolute residual below 1e-9 in floating point.

items.scope: Bounded scope: the stated concrete matrix and permutations only; rank preservation is verified for this instance, not proved in general.
items.statement: Row and column permutations of the concrete integer matrix [[1,2,3],[2,4,6],[1,1,1]] preserve its rank, which is 2, computed exactly over the rationals.

items.scope: UNSUPPORTED for machine check here: holographic duality is not established by any check in this package and no evidence for it is produced here; the bounded GEO checks above concern concrete grids, transforms, and shapes only.
items.statement: Recursive geometry in this engine is related to holographic duality.

families.title: Recursive Geometry (bounded checks on concrete arrays plus one abstract-only scope item)

honesty_rules: Machine-checkable MON items are checked only on a named finite instance (the symmetric group S3, realised as permutations of 3 elements). A finite instance is not the Monster group.
The Monster group itself appears only as abstract-only items; no enumeration or direct check of the Monster is performed anywhere in this package.
MOON data-checks use established published values only: the J-function coefficients 744, 196884, 21493760, 864299970 and McKay's identity 196884 = 196883 + 1.
GEO checks run on concrete arrays and grids only; their status is BOUNDED (bounded-scope numerical or exact evidence on the stated instance), never a general proof.
Abstract-only items are reported as UNSUPPORTED for machine check with the reason stated; they are never silently dropped.
